headline: At your yearly medication review, Dr. Smith kept your medicines the same and asked you to take old and borrowed pills to the pharmacy.

followUps.title: Take the disposal bag to the Elm Street pharmacy
followUps.detail: Bring the old amlodipine 10 mg pills, the expired naproxen, and the borrowed sleeping pills. Your current amlodipine dose is 5 mg.

followUps.title: Set up a weekly pill organizer
followUps.detail: Use one with a morning row and a night row. Lisa can fill it for you on Sundays.

followUps.title: Keep your appointment with Dr. Patel
followUps.detail: Your appointment is already arranged. No exact day or time was given at this visit.

followUps.title: Arrange your September visit with Dr. Smith
followUps.detail: Dr. Smith asked you to come back to the same clinic. No exact day or time was given.

instructions.text: Take lansoprazole 30 mg half an hour before breakfast. Don’t stop it suddenly. Dr. Smith said the acid can come back worse for a while.
Don’t take the borrowed sleeping pills. Dr. Smith said they raise your risk of falls and confusion at night.
Go to bed at the same time every night. Don’t nap after 3 p.m. or drink tea or coffee after lunch. Try decaf in the afternoon and get some daylight in the morning.

unchanged.text: Keep taking one ramipril 10 mg capsule each morning with breakfast.
Keep taking amlodipine 5 mg once a day at night.
Keep taking one atorvastatin 20 mg tablet at night.
Keep taking lansoprazole 30 mg once a day before breakfast for now.
Keep taking vitamin D, 1,000 units once a day with breakfast.
Keep using acetaminophen 500 mg tablets as needed for your knee. You can take up to 2 tablets at a time, up to 3 times a day. Don’t take more than 3,000 mg in a day.

openQuestions.text: Will you lower your lansoprazole dose?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: In fall 2026, you and Dr. Smith will talk about lowering the dose one step at a time.

openQuestions.text: Will you need more help with sleep?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: If you’re still having trouble sleeping, tell Dr. Smith at your next visit.
